51253957.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to hemagglutinin by SPR assay

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: Having speculated HA (HA2) as the potential target, we then characterized the affinity between HA and 6 by a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay with a view to clarifying whether HA protein was targeted. According to the SPR assay, we found that 6 could bind tightly to the HA immobilized on the CM5 chip with the calculated Kd value of 16.1 nM (Fig. 5A). This suggests that 6 was able to target HA protein and thus blocks the interactions of viruses with host cells, consistent with the result of inhibiting the entry of H5N1 pseudovirus. It seemed likely that 6 was able to bind to HA2 protein more tightly than HA owing to its remarkably improved Kd value of 0.17 nM delivered by 6 (Fig. 5B), revealing that targeting the HA2 domain has a significant effect on interaction between 6 and HA.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Fig. 5. Interaction of compound 6 with HA (A) and HA2 subunit (B) detected by SPR.
